# edgeos_nat_rule (Resource)

One NAT rule (`service nat rule <number>`).

There are three kinds of rule:

- `destination` rewrites the destination of packets arriving on `inbound_interface` to `inside_address` (DNAT, what a port forward does).
- `source` rewrites the source of packets leaving through `outbound_interface` to `outside_address` (SNAT).
- `masquerade` rewrites the source to the address of `outbound_interface`, the usual rule for a WAN link with a dynamic address.

Rules are evaluated in ascending order. The EdgeOS web UI keeps destination rules in 1 to 4999 and source and masquerade rules in 5000 to 9999; the provider warns when a rule is outside its range because the UI then shows it in the wrong list. Rules created by `port-forward` are separate and are not visible here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Masquerade everything leaving through the WAN port.
resource "edgeos_nat_rule" "masquerade" {
  number             = 5000
  type               = "masquerade"
  description        = "LAN to WAN"
  outbound_interface = "eth0"
}

# Send HTTPS arriving on the WAN address to a server on the LAN.
resource "edgeos_nat_rule" "web" {
  number            = 10
  type              = "destination"
  description       = "HTTPS to the web server"
  inbound_interface = "eth0"
  protocol          = "tcp"

  destination = {
    address = "203.0.113.2"
    port    = "443"
  }

  inside_address = {
    address = "192.168.1.20"
    port    = "8443"
  }
}

# Give the server VLAN its own public address.
resource "edgeos_nat_rule" "servers" {
  number             = 5010
  type               = "source"
  description        = "Server VLAN out through 203.0.113.10"
  outbound_interface = "eth0"

  source = {
    address = "192.168.20.0/24"
  }

  outside_address = {
    address = "203.0.113.10"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `number` (Number) Rule number from 1 to 9999. Changing it creates a new rule.
- `type` (String) `destination`, `source` or `masquerade`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free text description.
- `destination` (Attributes) Match on the destination of the packet. For a `destination` rule this is usually the WAN address and the public port. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination))
- `disabled` (Boolean) Keep the rule in the config but switch it off (the `disable` node). Defaults to `false`.
- `exclude` (Boolean) Exclude matching packets from NAT (the `exclude` node). Later rules are not evaluated for them. An exclude rule does not need a translation address. Defaults to `false`.
- `inbound_interface` (String) Interface the packets arrive on, such as `eth0` or `pppoe0`. Required for `destination` rules and not allowed for the other types.
- `inside_address` (Attributes) Where a `destination` rule sends the packets. Required for `destination` rules unless `exclude` is set, not allowed for the other types. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--inside_address))
- `log` (Boolean) Log packets matching this rule. Unset leaves the EdgeOS default (no logging).
- `outbound_interface` (String) Interface the packets leave through. Required for `source` and `masquerade` rules and not allowed for `destination` rules.
- `outside_address` (Attributes) What a `source` rule rewrites the source to. Required for `source` rules unless `exclude` is set, not allowed for `destination` and `masquerade` rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--outside_address))
- `protocol` (String) Protocol to match, such as `tcp`, `udp`, `tcp_udp` or `all`. Unset matches all protocols. Matching or translating ports needs `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`.
- `source` (Attributes) Match on the source of the packet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The rule number.

<a id="nestedatt--destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address, network (`192.0.2.0/24`) or range (`192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20`). Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `address_group` (String) Name of a firewall address group to match.
- `network_group` (String) Name of a firewall network group to match.
- `port` (String) Port, range, service name or comma separated list, such as `22`, `8000-8080` or `http,https`. Needs `protocol` `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`.
- `port_group` (String) Name of a firewall port group to match.


<a id="nestedatt--inside_address"></a>
### Nested Schema for `inside_address`

Required:

- `address` (String) Inside address, network or range, such as `192.168.1.10`.

Optional:

- `port` (String) Port or port range to translate to, such as `443` or `8000-8010`. Needs `protocol` `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`.


<a id="nestedatt--outside_address"></a>
### Nested Schema for `outside_address`

Required:

- `address` (String) Outside address, network or range, such as `203.0.113.10` or `203.0.113.8/29`.

Optional:

- `port` (String) Port or port range to translate to, such as `443` or `8000-8010`. Needs `protocol` `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`.


<a id="nestedatt--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address, network (`192.0.2.0/24`) or range (`192.0.2.10-192.0.2.20`). Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `address_group` (String) Name of a firewall address group to match.
- `network_group` (String) Name of a firewall network group to match.
- `port` (String) Port, range, service name or comma separated list, such as `22`, `8000-8080` or `http,https`. Needs `protocol` `tcp`, `udp` or `tcp_udp`.
- `port_group` (String) Name of a firewall port group to match.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = edgeos_nat_rule.example
  id = "5000"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import edgeos_nat_rule.example '5000'
```
